correctness.rationale: The support-function formula characterizes exact disk ranges by trace and square-zero Frobenius norm; a directly checked traceless 2-by-2 identity produces orthogonal top singular vectors for every input; Cauchy--Schwarz supplies an attained global lower bound, equality cases prove unique iff nonnormal, and real symmetric-part crossing establishes a real minimizer. All quantifiers (complex input/center, positive radius; real input/real center) and degenerate normal/scalar cases are explicit. Exact 1386 rational and 32810 complex numerical checks supplement but do not replace the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact fixed-center, fixed-radius numerical-range disk projection, complete normal/nonnormal minimizer multiplicity, and reality of a minimizer for real data were not found in inspected full-text nearness papers or queried mathematical records. Standard elliptical range and SVD theorems imply supporting ingredients but do not themselves state the simultaneous circular-range constraint or its exact projection/equality cases. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not independent proof of historical priority.
residual_risks: A classical theorem on nearest nilpotent orbits at prescribed norm may yield the same statement under a different name; targeted search is not an exhaustive literature census.
Two related published record full artifacts were not accessible; their retrieved claims target compressions rather than this projection, but undisclosed results could change priority.
An earlier paper combining elliptical-range geometry with constrained rank-one SVD may make this exact disk projection a corollary, even without a matching title.

The free-radius singularity corollary can be derived from classical SVD and is not asserted to have independent novelty; originality rests on the fixed positive radius, complete minimizers, and real-data guarantee.
The target is a single unitary orbit, and an older unitary-conjugacy Procrustes theorem might already evaluate its nearest-point distance.

value.rationale: A complete closed-form nonconvex matrix-nearness projection onto a naturally prescribed field-of-values disk is a motivated numerical-linear-algebra invariant, computed via a single SVD. Exact normal-versus-nonnormal uniqueness and real-data solvability distinguish it from ordinary unconstrained rank-one approximation and supply a calibration case for numerical-range repair algorithms. It does not claim larger-dimensional, spectral-norm, or floating-point-stability generalizations.
